rationale: The buyer is a marketing manager or competitive intelligence analyst at an SMB or agency — a specific named professional role at businesses that already pay $100–400/month for SEMrush or Ahrefs, confirming real willingness to pay for this category. The pain recurs daily (they're doing manual Google site: searches every day), the gap between Google Alerts and actual indexing is documented and widely experienced, and a focused $20–40/mo tool positioned as 'reliable Google Alerts for competitors' is meaningfully cheaper than the full-suite alternatives. Buildability is strong: automated site: search polling, URL deduplication, and daily email digests are achievable with Claude + scheduled scripts + email delivery. Operational autonomy scores 8 because once configured, delivery is fully automated — the operator only approves outreach batches. All build gates are met.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a competitor content tracker: it polls daily Google site: searches for domains you specify and emails you a digest of newly indexed URLs you haven't seen before, at a fraction of the cost of Ahrefs Alerts. The factory builds this as a Claude-powered scheduled job that runs daily site: queries (via a search API such as SerpAPI or ValueSERP), deduplicates against a stored URL history in SQLite, formats a clean email digest, and sends it via SendGrid — all wired together without Youval writing any code. To sell, the factory identifies marketing managers and growth/SEO leads at SMBs and agencies through LinkedIn (job title + company size filters) and drafts personalized outreach emails for Youval to approve before sending; the pitch is 'get reliable daily competitor content alerts for $29/mo instead of paying $400/mo for Ahrefs.' Once a customer signs up via a Stripe payment link, their monitored domains are added to the job queue automatically; Claude handles support queries by drafting replies for Youval to approve. The only recurring human step is approving outreach batches and reviewing flagged support tickets.
notes: All build gates passed: operational_autonomy=8, buildability_with_ai=8, buyer_clarity=7, willingness_to_pay=7. Main risk is scraping/search API terms of service — ensure chosen search API (e.g. ValueSERP) explicitly permits this use case. Defensibility is low (easily cloned) so move fast on customer acquisition.
